div.head: VIII Atr 22
div.ab: Gif man freondleasne weofodþén mid tihtlan belecge, þe adfultum næbbe, gá to corsnǽde ⁊ þar þonne æt gefare þæt þæt God wille, buton he on husle ladian mote.
Gif man freondleasne weofodþen mid tihtlan belecge, þe aðfultum næbbe, ga to corsnæde, and þar þonne æt gefare þæt þæt God wille, buton he on husle ladian mote.

If an accusation is brought against a minister of the altar who has no friends and no-one to support his oath, he shall go to the ordeal of consecrated bread, and shall experience there what is the will of God, unless he is allowed to clear himself by the Holy Communion.

If an accusation is brought against a friendless cleric who serves at the altar, one who does not have supporters for his oath, he shall undergo the ordeal of consecrated bread, and there endure whatever God wills, unless he is permitted to exonerate himself by the sacrament.

And if a minister of the altar who is without friends and who has no oath-helpers is accused, he is to go to the ordeal of the consecrated morsel, and then experience there what God wishes, unless he is allowed to clear himself on the host.

Wenn ein Altardiener, der keine Freunde [und Sippe und daher] keine Eideshilfe besitzt, mit Anklage belegt wird, so schreite er zum [Ordal des] Entscheidungsbissens und erfahre [d. h. leide] dann dabei das, was Gott will, ausser wenn er Erlaubniss erhält, im Abendmahlsgenuss sich zu reinigen.

If a servant of the altar who has no friends [or kin, and so] no oath-helpers is charged with an accusation, let him go to the [ordeal of the] consecrated morsel, and then experience [i.e. suffer] there what God wills, unless he is permitted to clear himself by [taking] the sacrament.
div.note: ordeal of consecrated bread: An ordeal in which the accused was required to swallow a portion of bread, which if it caught in his throat was taken as a sign of guilt.
